title: Type-Checker Exponential Explosion (Nested Lets)
pattern: The codebase contains deeply nested sequences of generic `let` bindings where each binding is substituted or nested inside the right-hand side of another binding, especially when working with heavily generic closures or type reconstruction.
why_bad: While locally appearing mathematically pure or elegant, it triggers a catastrophic compiler performance blowout. The Hindley-Milner type reconstruction algorithm (and Rust's type inference) has exponential worst-case complexity when handling deeply nested expressions. The compiler can spend minutes or hours attempting to prove the types, blowing up compile times and rendering iterative development impossible.
detection: Deeply nested closures or generics in let bindings where type inference is forced to trace type relationships across many levels of recursive right-hand-side substitutions.
counterexample: Standard linear sequences of let bindings are perfectly fine and compile instantly.
source: Benjamin C. Pierce, *Types and Programming Languages*, Chapter 22 "Type Reconstruction" (p. 336).
